# Deck cut sheet

*Generated by `sim/studies/deck_cut_sheet.py` — do not edit by hand. Re-run it if R₀ or the station layout changes.*

```
CableCell deck - cut sheet
==============================================================

Material: 1/2" plywood or MDF (12 mm nominal). Void-free ply if you
have it - the station bolts land near the top face.

feature                                   inches           mm
--------------------------------------------------------------
Outside diameter                        22-1/16"     560.0 mm
Thickness                                   1/2"      12.0 mm
Centre clearance hole                         7"     177.8 mm
Station bolt circle diameter             15-3/4"     400.0 mm
Mounts above bench top                    6-7/8"     174.0 mm

STATION POSITIONS - 7 stops on the bolt circle
Angles from S1, positive counter-clockwise viewed from above.

stop              angle     chord from S1
--------------------------------------------------------------
s1 feed            0.0 deg             0"
s2 slit           32.8 deg        4-7/16"
s3 strip          65.6 deg        8-9/16"
s4 crimp         118.6 deg       13-9/16"
s5 insert        171.5 deg      15-11/16"
s6 drop          204.4 deg        15-3/8"
s6 reject        237.2 deg      13-13/16"

Chord = straight-line distance from the S1 hole across the face.
Easier to lay out with a tape than to protract an angle.

PER-STATION HOLES - 4 per stop
  Rectangle 1-1/8" radial x 1-9/16" tangential
  (28 x 40 mm), centred on the bolt circle at each angle.
  Drill 1/4" (6.5 mm) clearance for M5 hardware.
  The printed station mounts are slotted radially, so a little
  drift is absorbed at assembly.

PRESS SCALLOP
  The press body crosses the disc at the S4 stop (118.6 deg).
  Cut a scallop 8-1/4" wide, inward from the
  rim to roughly 5-7/8" from centre.
  Cut it OVERSIZE and fit to the real press when it arrives - the
  ram-axis depth is still unmeasured.

TOLERANCE
  Bolt-circle diameter within +/- 1/16" is fine. The station mounts are
  slotted, and every station's height is calibrated in software at
  commissioning - the wood is not holding the precision.
```
